events.title: Henry IV at Canossa
events.shortBlurb: The excommunicated emperor Henry IV stood as a penitent in the snow before Pope Gregory VII to beg absolution…
body: In the last week of January 1077 the German king Henry IV, excommunicated and losing the support of his princes, crossed the winter Alps and came to the castle of Canossa in northern Italy, where Pope Gregory VII was staying. There, according to the accounts of the time, the king waited outside the gate for three days as a barefoot penitent in the snow.

On 28 January Gregory at last received him and lifted the excommunication, and the scene became the enduring symbol of a king humbled before the spiritual power of the Church. Yet the reconciliation was short-lived, and the long struggle between empire and papacy over the investiture of bishops continued for decades.
